find:
if (opener instanceof HTMLButtonElement && opener.disabled) return;
    if (isHiddenWithin(opener, el)) return;
why: EQUIVALENT since jsdom 30.1.2, and measured: it was `killed` under 30.1.1 and SURVIVED the bump (0 of 152). Without the guard, Back calls `focus()` on an opener the surface no longer shows -- the Levels button after `setLevelSelect(1, 1)` hid it while the pane was up. `isHiddenWithin` tests only `display: none` up to the HUD root, and an element under `display: none` is not focusable: browsers always refused it, and jsdom does from 30.1.2. So the refused `focus()` leaves focus where `setState` already put it, on the destination's own arrival (its primary action since issue #919), which is what "Back falls back to the menu's own arrival when the opener was hidden while the pane was up" asserts. The guard stays: it states the rule in the code rather than leaving it to the platform, and widening `isHiddenWithin` to a hiding the platform still focuses (zero opacity, off-screen) is what would flip this back to killed.
